posts.title: Why I’m building our own scheduling tool
posts.summary: Buffer works well for us today. Here’s why AUR Ventures is building its own anyway.
posts.body:
Right now AUR Studio schedules posts with Buffer, and it does the job. So why build our own?

## Subscriptions grow with you

Every new client means more accounts, more seats and a bigger monthly bill. For a young studio, that cost climbs faster than revenue. Owning the tool turns an ever-growing subscription into something we control.

## Built around how we work

Off-the-shelf tools are made for everyone. Ours can be shaped around the way the studio plans, approves and publishes content, without paying for features we never use.

## Starting small

The first version focuses on three platforms:

- Instagram
- LinkedIn
- X

It’s designed for mobile first, because that’s where most of my day-to-day social work happens.

## What comes next

We’ll use it daily inside the studio, fix what’s missing, then apply for official platform API approval. If it works as well as I hope, we may open it up to other teams too. I’ll share progress here as it happens.

posts.title: What makes a community feel looked after
posts.summary: Lessons from growing communities across several platforms: voice, speed and closing the loop.
posts.body:
Followers watch. Community members talk back, to the brand and to each other. Getting from one to the other comes down to a few habits.

## One voice, everywhere

Members notice when replies sound like different people. A consistent brand voice across platforms tells people someone is paying attention.

## Speed matters

A quick, thoughtful reply does more for trust than a perfect one a day later. Improving response times was one of the biggest drivers of engagement in my work at Bitgoro Media.

## Close the loop

When members share feedback, pass it to the team and tell members what changed. People keep contributing when they can see their ideas go somewhere.

## Set guardrails early

Clear guidelines and a plan for difficult questions protect the community. In healthcare, that means routing clinical questions to qualified staff, never answering them in a comment thread.

None of this is complicated. It just has to happen every day.
